  1297	\begin{lemma}[The sub-line distribution]
  1298		\label{lem:qld-sublines}
  1299		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SubLineWitness, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_subLineWitness}
  1300		\notready
  1301		\uses{def:line, def:line-point-dist, def:ith-restricted-line}
  1302		% Statement as in the source (references/qpbt-paper/
  1303		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, lem:qld-sublines). The
  1304		% line-point distribution over F_q^{2m+2} is built from the index
  1305		% function chi of def:ld-question-distribution at dimension 2m+2, which
  1306		% is defined only when 2m+2 divides q; the source instantiates it
  1307		% without securing this condition. See rem:qld-4-7-divisibility.
  1308		There exists a distribution $D$
  1309		over tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, where $\ell$ is a line in
  1310		$\F_q^{2m+2}$ and $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ are lines in $\F_q^m$, with the
  1311		following properties:
  1312		\begin{enumerate}
  1313			\item The marginal distribution over $\ell$ is the same as the
  1314			marginal of the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
  1315			% The source phrases the next property as: the marginal over
  1316			% (ell_X, ell_Z) is "a mixture of the product distributions
  1317			% D_{ALine,i} x D_{ALine,j} and D_{DLine,i} x D_{DLine,j}". Those
  1318			% products are distributions over pairs of line-point pairs, not
  1319			% over pairs of lines, so the phrase does not define the asserted
  1320			% marginal distribution on pairs of lines as written; the
  1321			% formulation below states the mixture at the level of the joint
  1322			% law of (ell_X, ell_Z, u), which is what the proofs of
  1323			% lem:claim-17-2 and lem:claim-17-3 use.
  1324			\item For any point of the form $u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$
  1325			lying on $\ell$, it holds that $u_X \in \ell_X$ and
  1326			$u_Z \in \ell_Z$. Moreover, the joint distribution of
  1327			$(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$, for $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z) \sim D$ and
  1328			$u$ chosen uniformly at random on $\ell$, is a mixture of
  1329			components indexed by a type
  1330			$\mathrm{v} \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and indices
  1331			$i, j \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ with the following two properties
  1332			within the component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$: the pair
  1333			$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is distributed according to the product of the
  1334			marginal distributions on lines of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and of
  1335			$D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the
  1336			point $u_X$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_X$ and likewise the
  1337			point $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_Z$. Equivalently,
  1338			since under each restricted distribution the point is uniformly
  1339			distributed on the line conditionally on the line: within the
  1340			component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$, the pair
  1341			$((\ell_X, u_X), (\ell_Z, z'))$, where $z'$ is a uniformly random
  1342			point of $\ell_Z$ sampled independently of $u$, is distributed
  1343			according to $D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and
  1344			symmetrically the pair $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, u_Z))$, with $x'$
  1345			a uniformly random point of $\ell_X$ sampled independently of
  1346			$u$, is distributed according to
  1347			$D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$. (No assertion is made
  1348			about the joint conditional law of the pair $(u_X, u_Z)$.)
  1349			\item If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, then $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are
  1350			axis-parallel.
  1351		\end{enumerate}
  1352		(Property~3 is not part of the numbered statement in the source; see
  1353		Remark~\ref{rem:qld-sublines-property-three}.)
  1354	\end{lemma}
  1355	\begin{proof}
  1356		\uses{def:line-representative, def:ld-question-distribution,
  1357			def:line-point-dist, def:ith-restricted-line, def:line,
  1358			prop:line-equiv}
  1359		The distribution $D$ is described by a sampling procedure. First sample
  1360		$(\ell, u)$ from the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and write
  1361		$u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$, so that Property~1 holds by
  1362		construction; all auxiliary randomness introduced below is sampled
  1363		independently of $(\ell, u)$. We write $\chi$ for the index function of
  1364		Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} at dimension $m$, whose
  1365		classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ for $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ partition $\F_q$
  1366		into sets of equal size $q/m$, and $\chi_{2m+2}$ for the index function
  1367		at dimension $2m+2$. The function $\chi_{2m+2}$, and with it the
  1368		line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ from which $(\ell, u)$ is
  1369		drawn, is defined only when $2m+2$ divides $q$
  1370		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}); admissibility of
  1371		$(q,m,d)$ supplies only that $m$ divides $q$, and for admissible
  1372		parameters with $m \ge 2$ the required divisibility fails, so this
  1373		first step is an unresolved obligation of the source argument, recorded
  1374		in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and analyzed in
  1375		\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; the construction below is
  1376		carried out for the parameters for which the distribution is defined.
  1377		By a
  1378		\emph{fresh diagonal direction pair} we mean a pair $(s', w')$ with
  1379		$s'$ uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $w' \in \F_q^m$ having coordinates
  1380		$1, \dots, \chi(s')-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates
  1381		uniformly random; this is exactly the law of the coordinate--direction
  1382		data of the diagonal component of the line-point distribution over
  1383		$\F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}).
  1384	
  1385		If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, $\ell = (v, e_j)$ with
  1386		$v = (v_X, v_Z, \alpha_0, \beta_0)$ and $j \in \{1, \dots, 2m+2\}$, set
  1387		$\ell_X = (v'_X, e_{i_X})$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, e_{i_Z})$ where: for
  1388		$1 \le j \le m$, $i_X = j$ and $i_Z$ is uniformly random in
  1389		$\{1,\dots,m\}$; for $m+1 \le j \le 2m$, $i_X$ is uniformly random and
  1390		$i_Z = j - m$; for $2m+1 \le j \le 2m+2$, both $i_X$ and $i_Z$ are
  1391		uniformly random; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are the canonical line
  1392		representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the chosen directions
  1393		(Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}), so that $v_X \in \ell_X$
  1394		and $v_Z \in \ell_Z$.
  1395	
  1396		If $\ell$ is diagonal, $\ell = (v, s, w)$, then by the construction of
  1397		the diagonal component of the line-point distribution
  1398		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} instantiated at
  1399		dimension $2m+2$) the direction $w = (w_X, w_Z, \gamma, \delta)$ has
  1400		coordinates $1, \dots, j-1$ equal to $0$, where $j = \chi_{2m+2}(s)$,
  1401		and its remaining coordinates are uniformly random. These remaining
  1402		coordinates may also vanish, so $w$ need not have a nonzero coordinate
  1403		at index $j$ and may be the zero vector, in which case $\ell$ is a
  1404		singleton (Definition~\ref{def:line}).
  1405		% The source proof describes w as "a direction vector whose first
  1406		% nonzero coordinate is j = chi(s)"
  1407		% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, proof
  1408		% of lem:qld-sublines); the distribution delivers only the weaker
  1409		% property recorded here, which is the one the argument uses. The
  1410		% source also leaves the laws of s_X and s_Z unspecified ("chosen such
  1411		% that chi(s_X) = j"); the uniform choices below are needed for the
  1412		% exact marginals claimed in Property 2.
  1413		Sample $\ell_X = (v'_X, s_X, w'_X)$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, s_Z, w'_Z)$
  1414		where: for $1 \le j \le m$, $w'_X = w_X$ and $w'_Z = w_Z$, with $s_X$
  1415		uniformly random in the class $\chi^{-1}(j)$ and $s_Z$ uniformly
  1416		random in the class $\chi^{-1}(1)$; for $m+1 \le j \le 2m$, the pair
  1417		$(s_X, w'_X)$ is a fresh diagonal direction pair and $w'_Z = w_Z$,
  1418		with $s_Z$ uniformly random in the class $\chi^{-1}(j-m)$; for
  1419		$2m+1 \le j \le 2m+2$, both $(s_X, w'_X)$ and $(s_Z, w'_Z)$ are fresh
  1420		diagonal direction pairs, sampled independently; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are
  1421		the canonical representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the directions
  1422		$w'_X, w'_Z$.
  1423	
  1424		Property~3 is immediate from the procedure: when $\ell$ is
  1425		axis-parallel, both $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are constructed to be
  1426		axis-parallel. The containments in Property~2 hold for every point
  1427		$u^\dagger = (u^\dagger_X, u^\dagger_Z, \alpha^\dagger,
  1428		\beta^\dagger)$ of $\ell$: the block $u^\dagger_X$ differs from $v_X$
  1429		by a multiple of the direction of $\ell_X$ when that direction is
  1430		inherited from $\ell$ (namely $e_j$ for axis-parallel $\ell$ with
  1431		$1 \le j \le m$, and $w_X$ for diagonal $\ell$ with $1 \le j \le m$),
  1432		and equals $v_X$ in all other cases, since then the corresponding
  1433		block of the direction of $\ell$ vanishes; in either case
  1434		$u^\dagger_X \in \ell_X$ because $v_X \in \ell_X$, and symmetrically
  1435		$u^\dagger_Z \in \ell_Z$.
  1436	
  1437		For the distributional part of Property~2, observe first that
  1438		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is a function of $\ell$ and of the auxiliary
  1439		randomness alone: the directions used are either read off from the
  1440		direction data of $\ell$ or freshly sampled, and by
  1441		Proposition~\ref{prop:line-equiv} the canonical representatives
  1442		$v'_X, v'_Z$ do not depend on which base point of $\ell$ is used to
  1443		compute them. Under both components of the line-point distribution the
  1444		point $u$ is uniformly distributed on $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and, conditioned
  1445		on the line $\ell$, uniformly distributed on the points of $\ell$
  1446		(each of the $q$ values of the line parameter, or the single point
  1447		when the direction vanishes, being equally likely). Hence, conditioned
  1448		on $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the sampled point $u$ is uniformly
  1449		distributed on $\ell$, and it suffices to establish the claimed
  1450		mixture description for the tuple $(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$ produced by
  1451		the procedure itself.
  1452	
  1453		Condition on the component of the line-point distribution
  1454		(axis-parallel or diagonal) and on $j$; the mixture of Property~2 is
  1455		over these choices together with the fresh index choices, and the
  1456		blocks $u_X, u_Z$ of $u$ are independent and uniform on $\F_q^m$,
  1457		independent of all direction data. In the axis-parallel case with
  1458		$1 \le j \le m$, the pair $(\ell_X, u_X)$ consists of the uniformly
  1459		random point $u_X$ together with the canonical axis-parallel line
  1460		through it in direction $e_j$, so
  1461		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},j}$, while, conditioned
  1462		additionally on $i_Z$, the pair $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ consists of the
  1463		uniformly random point $u_Z$ together with the canonical line through
  1464		it in direction $e_{i_Z}$, so
  1465		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},i_Z}$; the two pairs are
  1466		functions of the disjoint independent data $u_X$ and $(u_Z, i_Z)$,
  1467		hence independent. In the diagonal case with $1 \le j \le m$, the
  1468		triple $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ has $u_X$ uniform, $w_X$ with coordinates
  1469		$1, \dots, j-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates uniform,
  1470		and $s_X$ uniform in $\chi^{-1}(j)$, which is exactly the law
  1471		generating $D_{\mathrm{DLine},j}$; hence
  1472		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},j}$, and similarly
  1473		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},1}$ since $w_Z$ is uniform and
  1474		$s_Z$ is uniform in $\chi^{-1}(1)$; the two pairs are functions of the
  1475		disjoint independent data $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ and $(u_Z, w_Z, s_Z)$,
  1476		hence independent. The remaining cases are analogous: each of
  1477		$(\ell_X, u_X)$ and $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ is either built from the inherited
  1478		direction block as above, or from a fresh axis index or fresh diagonal
  1479		direction pair, in which case it is distributed as the uniform mixture
  1480		over $i$ of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ for the corresponding type
  1481		$\mathrm{v}$; and the two pairs are always functions of disjoint
  1482		independent collections of the variables $u_X$, $u_Z$, the direction
  1483		blocks, and the fresh auxiliary choices, hence independent conditioned
  1484		on the component. Within each component this yields exactly the
  1485		description of Property~2: the pair $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is
  1486		product-distributed according to the line marginals of
  1487		$D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and $D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on
  1488		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, each of $u_X$ and $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed
  1489		on its line, because under each restricted distribution the point is
  1490		uniform on the line conditionally on the line. The equivalent product
  1491		formulations follow from the same conditional uniformity.
  1492	\end{proof}
  1493	
  1494	\begin{remark}[Property~3 of the sub-line distribution]
  1495		\label{rem:qld-sublines-property-three}
  1496		The source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13} in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}
  1497		appeals to a ``Property~3'' of the sub-line lemma, while the statement
  1498		given there lists only two numbered properties, so the reference is
  1499		dangling. The intended assertion is the axis-parallel closure property

  1501		immediate from the sampling procedure in the proof.
  1502	\end{remark}

  1509	registers $\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''$, and the sums range over
  1510	$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$.

/-!
# Weighted collision bounds for sampled lines

This module lifts the uniform affine-parameter collision estimate to the mixed
line-point distribution with an arbitrary nonnegative weight depending only on
the sampled line.

## References

The estimate is the Schwartz--Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- The collision bound remains valid with any nonnegative weight depending
only on the line, after restricting to nonzero directions. This proof-only
estimate is the conditional form of the root argument in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
paper lines 950--955; it does not assert the false unrestricted collision bound
on zero-direction coefficient presentations. -/
theorem linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le {L : LdParams}
    {bound : ℕ} (weight : LineDesc L → ℝ)
    (hweight : ∀ line, 0 ≤ weight line) (first second : DegPoly L bound)
    (hne : first ≠ second) :
    avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
      if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight sample.1 *
        (if evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 first = evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 second
          then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
      (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) *
        avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
          if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight sample.1 else 0) := by
  classical
  rw [avgOver_linePointDist_resample_parameter]
  rw [← avgOver_const_mul]
  apply avgOver_mono
  intro sample
  by_cases hdir : sample.1.direction ≠ 0
  · simp only [if_pos hdir]
    rw [avgOver_const_mul]
    exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
      (evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le sample.1 hdir first second hne)
      (hweight sample.1)).trans_eq
      (mul_comm _ _)
  · simp [hdir, avgOver]

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.AffineEvaluation
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.PolynomialCollision

/-!
# Uniform collision bounds on nondegenerate affine lines

This module combines uniqueness of affine evaluation with the univariate
root-count bound to control collisions under a uniform line parameter.

## References

The result is the Schwartz--Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

noncomputable section

/-- On a nondegenerate line, completed evaluations of distinct degree-bounded
polynomials collide with probability at most the degree bound divided by the
field size under a uniform affine parameter. -/
theorem evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le {L : LdParams} {bound : ℕ}
    (line : LineDesc L) (hdir : line.direction ≠ 0)
    (first second : DegPoly L bound) (hne : first ≠ second) :
    avgOver (uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L)) (fun param =>
      if evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) first =
        evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) second then 1 else 0) ≤
      (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) := by
  classical
  simp_rw [evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero line hdir,
    Option.some.injEq]
  have hcard := evalCoefficient_collision_card_le first second hne
  unfold avgOver
  simp only [uniformDistribution_support, uniformDistribution_weight_apply,
    mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero, ← Finset.sum_filter]
  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one_div]
  exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hcard) (by positivity)

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.RestrictedAverage
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Lines.WeightedCollision

/-!
# Product-distribution weighted collision bounds

This module lifts the nondegenerate weighted collision estimate for one
line-point sample to two independent samples. The nonnegative weight may
depend on the complete second sample and on the first sampled line.

## References

This is formalization-only conditioning support for `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`, using
the collision hypothesis of `lem:pasting` at
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- Independent sampling of a second line-point pair preserves the weighted
collision estimate on nonzero first directions. The weight may depend on the
complete second sample, but on the first sample only through its line. No
condition is imposed on the second direction. -/
theorem prod_linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le
    {L : LdParams} {bound : ℕ}
    (weight : LineDesc L → (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) → ℝ)
    (hweight : ∀ line sample, 0 ≤ weight line sample)
    (first second : DegPoly L bound) (hne : first ≠ second) :
    avgOver (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)) (fun samples =>
      if samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight samples.1.1 samples.2 *
        (if evalOpt samples.1.1 samples.1.2 first =
          evalOpt samples.1.1 samples.1.2 second then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
    (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) *
      avgOver (Distribution.prod (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)) (fun samples =>
        if samples.1.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight samples.1.1 samples.2 else 0) := by
  classical
  simp only [avgOver_prod]
  rw [avgOver_comm, avgOver_comm (linePointDist L) (linePointDist L)
    (fun firstSample secondSample =>
      if firstSample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight firstSample.1 secondSample else 0)]
  rw [← avgOver_const_mul]
  apply avgOver_mono
  intro sample
  exact linePointDist_nondegenerate_weighted_collision_le
    (fun line => weight line sample) (fun line => hweight line sample)
    first second hne

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

abbrev SubLineTriple (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
  DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ×
    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams)

/-- An extended line tuple together with a point sampled uniformly on it. -/
abbrev SubLinePointSample (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
  SubLineTriple P ×
    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)

/-- The shared restricted line kind and two coordinate indices in one mixture
component of the subline law. -/
abbrev SubLineComponent (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
  LineKind × (Fin P.m × Fin P.m)

/-- Select the restricted line-point distribution of a given kind and index. -/
noncomputable def restrictedLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
    Distribution (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
  match kind with
  | .axis => restrictedALineDist P.toLdParams i
  | .diagonal => restrictedDLineDist P.toLdParams i

/-- Sample a subline tuple and then a uniform affine parameter on its
extended line. -/
noncomputable def subLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)) :
    Distribution (SubLinePointSample P) :=
  (Distribution.prod D
    (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).map fun sample =>
      (sample.1, sample.1.1.base + sample.2 • sample.1.1.direction)

/-- Retain the projected line pair and the X projection of an extended point. -/
def subLineXProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (sample : SubLinePointSample P) :
    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
  (sample.1.2, projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))

/-- Retain the projected line pair and the Z projection of an extended point. -/
def subLineZProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (sample : SubLinePointSample P) :
    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
  (sample.1.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))

/-- The X-point marginal associated with one restricted product component. -/
noncomputable def subLineXComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
    Distribution
      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
  (Distribution.prod
    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1)
    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2).map Prod.fst)).map
      fun sample => ((sample.1.1, sample.2), sample.1.2)

/-- The Z-point marginal associated with one restricted product component. -/
noncomputable def subLineZComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
    Distribution
      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
  (Distribution.prod
    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1).map Prod.fst)
    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2)).map
      fun sample => ((sample.1, sample.2.1), sample.2.2)

/-- Directly indexed form of the subline distribution of `lem:qld-sublines`,
paper lines 1063--1069.  Its extended-line marginal is the directly indexed
line-point law rather than the seed-indexed line-point distribution over
`F_q^(2m+2)` of the source statement; that replacement is documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`, so this is a
formalization auxiliary record, not the source-labelled statement.  Its
source-mixture field records the X and Z point marginals separately; it does
not assert a joint conditional law for the pair of projected points. -/
structure SubLineWitness (P : AdmissibleParams) where
  /-- The actual distribution of an extended line and two projected lines. -/
  D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)
  /-- The distribution has total mass one. -/
  isProbability : D.IsProbability
  /-- Its extended-line marginal is the direct line-point marginal. -/
  extended_marginal : D.map Prod.fst =
    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst
  /-- Every point of an extended line projects onto both stored source lines. -/
  incidence : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, ∀ u ∈ sample.1.pointSet,
    projX (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.1.pointSet ∧
      projZ (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.2.pointSet
  /-- Each line triple carries affine data sufficient for
  `combineLinePoly_spec`. -/
  compatibility : ∀ sample ∈ D.support,
    ∃ aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta : PauliScalar P,
      IsCombineLineCompatible
        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.base)
        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.direction)
        sample.2.1.base sample.2.1.direction
        sample.2.2.base sample.2.2.direction
        aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta
  /-- Each one-point projected marginal is a mixture of restricted product
  laws.  No equality for their joint conditional law is claimed. -/
  source_mixture : ∃ components : Distribution (SubLineComponent P),
    components.IsProbability ∧
      (subLinePointDist P D).map subLineXProjection =
        Distribution.bind components (subLineXComponentDist P) ∧
      (subLinePointDist P D).map subLineZProjection =
        Distribution.bind components (subLineZComponentDist P)
  /-- An extended axis line has axis-parallel projected lines. -/
  axis_closure : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, sample.1.kind = .axis ->
    sample.2.1.kind = .axis ∧ sample.2.2.kind = .axis

/-! ## Extended lines and global polynomial pairs -/

/-- Extended-line POVMs and directly indexed, completed-answer forms of the two
consistency relations in `lem:qld-4-13`, paper lines 1020--1034. The direct line
carrier avoids the dimension-divisibility obstruction documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`. -/
structure ExtendedLinesWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
    (δ : ℝ) where
  /-- The complete extended-line measurement on each player side. -/
  Qline : (side : PlayerSide) -> DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ->
    Measurement (DirectDegPoly P.extendedDirectLd (P.m * P.d + 1))
      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
  /-- Axis-line outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
